Virtual Try-On take-home — Ray Tan

Output Comparison vs the Magic Hour Website

Identical inputs across four configurations: raw Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 at defaults, the Magic Hour production output (downloaded straight from the Magic Hour AI Clothes Changer API, unmodified, native 384×576), and the two shipped implementations — Seedream single-model and the Seedream → Qwen-Image-3 realism-refine cascade.

12 test pairs. Every output was scored by a deterministic CV harness and a blind GPT-5.5 rubric judge; full boards and methodology in the repository README and report.

github.com/101011101/magichour_takehome · images unmodified, aspect ratios preserved
Summary — 12 grid pairs, both judges

Where each configuration lands

  • Website vs raw model: the production output (0.557 deterministic / 3.92 VLM) scores meaningfully above raw Qwen 2511 (0.404 / 3.83) — the website wrapper adds real value.
  • Ours vs website: on the blind VLM both shipped implementations rank above the production output (cascade 4.14, Seedream 4.08 vs 3.92); on pixel-preservation metrics Seedream (0.569) edges it while the cascade trades pixel fidelity for perceptual quality.
  • Website weak spots per the judges: lowest identity cosine of any arm (person replaced entirely on one pair) and garment accuracy 3.25 on the VLM.
  • On 18 held-out pairs (website not run — credit budget) the cascade ranked #1 on the blind VLM board (4.22) and beat its own stage-1 parent deterministically.
Deterministic composite: anchored per-output normalization, garment-fidelity weighted ×2 · VLM: six-criterion 1–5 rubric, model names hidden from the judge
